Pay the right fare

Compare the options before buying.

London fares are straightforward for a single adult journey but become less obvious for families, children, longer stays and trips crossing the Monday-to-Sunday weekly-capping period.

The calculator compares the main options using your group and visit details. It includes cash needed for Oyster cards, possible unused credit and cards you already own. No visitor details are stored.

Useful for
  • Families travelling with children
  • Visits lasting several days
  • Comparing Oyster and contactless
  • Understanding upfront cash needed
How to use it

Describe the visit, then compare.

  1. 01

    Describe your group

    Enter the number of adults and children, including children’s ages because London fare rules differ.

  2. 02

    Add travel dates

    Choose the first day and number of travel days so weekly capping can be considered.

  3. 03

    Add existing cards

    Include suitable Oyster cards already owned to avoid charging for unnecessary replacements.

  4. 04

    Compare totals

    Review estimated cost, cash required, card charges and likely unused Oyster credit.

What it includes

The main visitor options.

The comparison covers adult contactless daily and weekly capping, standard Oyster pay as you go, 7-Day Travelcards, eligible under-11 free travel and the 11–15 Young Visitor discount.

It also accounts for standard Oyster card costs, £5 top-up increments and cards the group already owns. Fare values are maintained separately when TfL prices change.

What to know

An independent planning estimate.

This is not a TfL sales or ticketing service. It does not cover every concession, Visitor Oyster, Zip Oyster or every unusual journey pattern.

The current comparison is designed mainly for Zones 1–2. Confirm eligibility, current prices and travel outside that scope with TfL before buying or loading credit.

Worked example

Comparing travel for a family visit.

Two adults are visiting for five days with children aged 10 and 13. They expect mainly Zones 1–2 travel and already own one standard Oyster card.

  1. Enter both adults and the children’s ages so the calculator can distinguish under-11 travel from the 11–15 rules.
  2. Add the arrival day and five-day duration. This matters because weekly capping runs Monday to Sunday rather than across any seven consecutive days.
  3. Record the Oyster card already owned so the comparison does not add an unnecessary card cost.
  4. Compare the estimated fare with the upfront cash requirement and possible unused Oyster credit; the cheapest headline is not always the simplest choice.

The useful result: a group-specific payment strategy based on current maintained inputs, followed by an eligibility check with TfL before purchase. Run the comparison again if the dates move across Sunday or the group adds airport and wider-zone journeys.

Common questions

Choosing between payment options.

Does the calculator always recommend contactless instead of Oyster?

No. It compares the supported options using the group, travel dates, children’s ages and cards already owned. The most practical option can change for families and visits crossing the Monday-to-Sunday weekly-capping period.

How are children handled?

The comparison accounts for eligible under-11 free travel and the 11–15 Young Visitor discount. Eligibility and how a discount is added should always be confirmed with TfL before travel.

Can I use the result for journeys outside Zones 1–2?

The calculator is designed mainly for typical visitor travel in Zones 1–2. Airport journeys, wider-zone travel and unusual patterns can change the best option, so check those separately with TfL.
